newsitem.title: UK: European group approves new coffee contract.
newsitem.headline: European group approves new coffee contract.

text.p: The European Coffee Federation (ECF) has approved a new standard coffee contract and revised three existing contracts to keep in line with industry trends.
The changes were endorsed at the ECF annual meeting in Vienna on Tuesday, according to an ECF statement on Wednesday. The ECF groups the region's roasters and traders.

The new European Delivery Contract for Coffee, which will enter into force this January 1, is designed to cover sales for future delivery at a European location. It would cater both for coffee shipped in bulk and in bags.
"It is felt that this will fill a gap in current trading methods," the statement said, without elaborating.
It said changes to the existing European Coffee Contract, established in 1956, include:
- A reduction in the weight franchise (the maximum acceptable loss in weight between shipped and arrival weights) to 0.5 percent from 1.0 percent.

- a stipulation that coffee bags must comply with the legal requirements for food packaging materials and waste management in the country of destination. This is in line with environmental laws in Europe.
Two other contracts -- the European Contract for Spot Coffee and The European Contract for Coffee in Bulk -- were also revised. -- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
